function.name: glob_files
function.description: Recursively list workspace-relative file paths that match a glob, in sorted order. The glob is matched against each file's relative path and against its file name, using Python fnmatch rules, case-sensitive: '*' and '?' also match '/', and '[abc]' matches one listed character. It never matches file contents. Cache and VCS directories (.git, __pycache__, .pytest_cache, .mypy_cache, .ruff_cache, .tox, .venv, node_modules) are skipped.

path.description: Directory (or single file) to list under, relative to the workspace root. Default '.'.

function.name: read_file
function.description: Read a text file with 1-based line numbers. start_line and end_line are inclusive; omit start_line to begin at line 1 and end_line to read to the end. The header reports the range returned and the file's total lines. Long results are shown partially with an output id for paging.

function.name: outline
function.description: List the classes and functions of a Python file with line numbers.

function.name: search_text
function.description: Search file contents for exact text (literal characters, case-sensitive; not a regex). Returns one line per match as path:line: text, with 1-based line numbers, and states the scope searched. file_glob only selects which files are searched.

query.description: Required. The exact text to find, e.g. 'def get_real_name('.

path.description: File or directory to search, relative to the workspace root. Default '.'.

file_glob.description: Optional glob selecting files by relative path or file name (same rules as glob_files), e.g. '*.py'. It never matches file contents. Default '*'.

function.name: replace_text
function.description: Replace exact text in a file. Fails without changing the file if old_text is absent, or if it occurs more than once while replace_all is false; set replace_all to replace every occurrence. Reports how many occurrences were replaced and shows the edited lines.

function.name: write_file
function.description: Create a file, or overwrite it completely if it already exists, with the given content. Missing parent directories are created. Paths are relative to the workspace root.

function.name: run
function.description: Run one command in the workspace root without a shell: no pipes, redirection, chaining (&&, ;), cd, or variable expansion; use workspace-relative paths with forward slashes. 'python' and 'pytest' use the task's Python environment. Shows the command, status (including timeout), exit code, stdout, and stderr; long output is shown partially with an output id for paging. A successful exit does not mean the task is accepted.

function.name: read_output
function.description: Read part of an earlier tool result by its output id (for example out_12). Results that were shown partially say which id and range to request. Give start_line/end_line, or start_byte/end_byte for very long lines.

function.name: search_output
function.description: Find lines containing a literal string (plain text, not a regex) in an earlier tool result by its output id.

query.description: Required. The literal text to find.

function.name: history
function.description: Page through authorized durable session history. The response includes a stable next_cursor.

function.name: search_history
function.description: Find literal text in authorized prior actions and observations without knowing an output ID.

function.name: read_artifact
function.description: Read an authorized session artifact by ID, optionally using an exact byte range.

function.name: note
function.description: Save a named plain-text note that persists across turns. Pinned notes are placed in context when space allows.

function.name: read_note
function.description: Read a saved note by name.

function.name: finish
function.description: Declare the work complete. The final workspace is then checked independently.

function.name: glob_files
function.description: Recursively list workspace-relative file paths that match a glob, in sorted order. The glob is matched against each file's relative path and against its file name, using Python fnmatch rules, case-sensitive: '*' and '?' also match '/', and '[abc]' matches one listed character. It never matches file contents. Cache and VCS directories (.git, __pycache__, .pytest_cache, .mypy_cache, .ruff_cache, .tox, .venv, node_modules) are skipped.

path.description: Directory (or single file) to list under, relative to the workspace root. Default '.'.

function.name: read_file
function.description: Read a text file with 1-based line numbers. start_line and end_line are inclusive; omit start_line to begin at line 1 and end_line to read to the end. The header reports the range returned and the file's total lines. Long results are shown partially with an output id for paging.

function.name: outline
function.description: List the classes and functions of a Python file with line numbers.

function.name: search_text
function.description: Search file contents for exact text (literal characters, case-sensitive; not a regex). Returns one line per match as path:line: text, with 1-based line numbers, and states the scope searched. file_glob only selects which files are searched.

query.description: Required. The exact text to find, e.g. 'def get_real_name('.

path.description: File or directory to search, relative to the workspace root. Default '.'.

file_glob.description: Optional glob selecting files by relative path or file name (same rules as glob_files), e.g. '*.py'. It never matches file contents. Default '*'.

function.name: replace_text
function.description: Replace exact text in a file. Fails without changing the file if old_text is absent, or if it occurs more than once while replace_all is false; set replace_all to replace every occurrence. Reports how many occurrences were replaced and shows the edited lines.

function.name: write_file
function.description: Create a file, or overwrite it completely if it already exists, with the given content. Missing parent directories are created. Paths are relative to the workspace root.

function.name: run
function.description: Run one command in the workspace root without a shell: no pipes, redirection, chaining (&&, ;), cd, or variable expansion; use workspace-relative paths with forward slashes. 'python' and 'pytest' use the task's Python environment. Shows the command, status (including timeout), exit code, stdout, and stderr; long output is shown partially with an output id for paging. A successful exit does not mean the task is accepted.

function.name: read_output
function.description: Read part of an earlier tool result by its output id (for example out_12). Results that were shown partially say which id and range to request. Give start_line/end_line, or start_byte/end_byte for very long lines.

function.name: search_output
function.description: Find lines containing a literal string (plain text, not a regex) in an earlier tool result by its output id.

query.description: Required. The literal text to find.

function.name: history
function.description: Page through authorized durable session history. The response includes a stable next_cursor.

function.name: search_history
function.description: Find literal text in authorized prior actions and observations without knowing an output ID.

function.name: read_artifact
function.description: Read an authorized session artifact by ID, optionally using an exact byte range.

function.name: note
function.description: Save a named plain-text note that persists across turns. Pinned notes are placed in context when space allows.

function.name: read_note
function.description: Read a saved note by name.

function.name: finish
function.description: Declare the work complete. The final workspace is then checked independently.

function.name: glob_files
function.description: Recursively list workspace-relative file paths that match a glob, in sorted order. The glob is matched against each file's relative path and against its file name, using Python fnmatch rules, case-sensitive: '*' and '?' also match '/', and '[abc]' matches one listed character. It never matches file contents. Cache and VCS directories (.git, __pycache__, .pytest_cache, .mypy_cache, .ruff_cache, .tox, .venv, node_modules) are skipped.

path.description: Directory (or single file) to list under, relative to the workspace root. Default '.'.

function.name: read_file
function.description: Read a text file with 1-based line numbers. start_line and end_line are inclusive; omit start_line to begin at line 1 and end_line to read to the end. The header reports the range returned and the file's total lines. Long results are shown partially with an output id for paging.

function.name: outline
function.description: List the classes and functions of a Python file with line numbers.

function.name: search_text
function.description: Search file contents for exact text (literal characters, case-sensitive; not a regex). Returns one line per match as path:line: text, with 1-based line numbers, and states the scope searched. file_glob only selects which files are searched.

query.description: Required. The exact text to find, e.g. 'def get_real_name('.

path.description: File or directory to search, relative to the workspace root. Default '.'.

file_glob.description: Optional glob selecting files by relative path or file name (same rules as glob_files), e.g. '*.py'. It never matches file contents. Default '*'.

function.name: replace_text
function.description: Replace exact text in a file. Fails without changing the file if old_text is absent, or if it occurs more than once while replace_all is false; set replace_all to replace every occurrence. Reports how many occurrences were replaced and shows the edited lines.

function.name: write_file
function.description: Create a file, or overwrite it completely if it already exists, with the given content. Missing parent directories are created. Paths are relative to the workspace root.

function.name: run
function.description: Run one command in the workspace root without a shell: no pipes, redirection, chaining (&&, ;), cd, or variable expansion; use workspace-relative paths with forward slashes. 'python' and 'pytest' use the task's Python environment. Shows the command, status (including timeout), exit code, stdout, and stderr; long output is shown partially with an output id for paging. A successful exit does not mean the task is accepted.

function.name: read_output
function.description: Read part of an earlier tool result by its output id (for example out_12). Results that were shown partially say which id and range to request. Give start_line/end_line, or start_byte/end_byte for very long lines.

function.name: search_output
function.description: Find lines containing a literal string (plain text, not a regex) in an earlier tool result by its output id.

query.description: Required. The literal text to find.

function.description: Find literal text in authorized prior actions and observations without knowing an output ID.

function.name: glob_files

The glob is matched against each file's relative path and against its file name, using Python fnmatch rules, case-sensitive: '*' and '?' also match '/', and '[abc]' matches one listed character. path.description: Directory (or single file) to list under, relative to the workspace root. Default '.'.

function.name: glob_files
function.description: Recursively list workspace-relative file paths that match a glob, in sorted order. The glob is matched against each file's relative path and against its file name, using Python fnmatch rules, case-sensitive: '*' and '?' also match '/', and '[abc]' matches one listed character. It never matches file contents. Cache and VCS directories (.git, __pycache__, .pytest_cache, .mypy_cache, .ruff_cache, .tox, .venv, node_modules) are skipped.

path.description: Directory (or single file) to list under, relative to the workspace root. Default '.'.

function.name: read_file
function.description: Read a text file with 1-based line numbers. start_line and end_line are inclusive; omit start_line to begin at line 1 and end_line to read to the end. The header reports the range returned and the file's total lines. Long results are shown partially with an output id for paging.

function.name: outline
function.description: List the classes and functions of a Python file with line numbers.

function.name: search_text
function.description: Search file contents for exact text (literal characters, case-sensitive; not a regex). Returns one line per match as path:line: text, with 1-based line numbers, and states the scope searched. file_glob only selects which files are searched.

query.description: Required. The exact text to find, e.g. 'def get_real_name('.

path.description: File or directory to search, relative to the workspace root. Default '.'.

file_glob.description: Optional glob selecting files by relative path or file name (same rules as glob_files), e.g. '*.py'. It never matches file contents. Default '*'.

function.name: replace_text
function.description: Replace exact text in a file. Fails without changing the file if old_text is absent, or if it occurs more than once while replace_all is false; set replace_all to replace every occurrence. Reports how many occurrences were replaced and shows the edited lines.

function.name: write_file
function.description: Create a file, or overwrite it completely if it already exists, with the given content. Missing parent directories are created. Paths are relative to the workspace root.

function.name: run
function.description: Run one command in the workspace root without a shell: no pipes, redirection, chaining (&&, ;), cd, or variable expansion; use workspace-relative paths with forward slashes. 'python' and 'pytest' use the task's Python environment. Shows the command, status (including timeout), exit code, stdout, and stderr; long output is shown partially with an output id for paging. A successful exit does not mean the task is accepted.

function.name: read_output
function.description: Read part of an earlier tool result by its output id (for example out_12). Results that were shown partially say which id and range to request. Give start_line/end_line, or start_byte/end_byte for very long lines.

function.name: search_output
function.description: Find lines containing a literal string (plain text, not a regex) in an earlier tool result by its output id.

query.description: Required. The literal text to find.

function.name: history
function.description: Page through authorized durable session history. The response includes a stable next_cursor.

function.name: search_history
function.description: Find literal text in authorized prior actions and observations without knowing an output ID.

function.name: read_artifact
function.description: Read an authorized session artifact by ID, optionally using an exact byte range.

function.name: note
function.description: Save a named plain-text note that persists across turns. Pinned notes are placed in context when space allows.

function.name: read_note
function.description: Read a saved note by name.

function.name: finish
function.description: Declare the work complete. The final workspace is then checked independently.

   10| Security Fixes
   11| 
   12| * Fix uncontrolled CPU consumption in ``TokenList`` grouping (CWE-1333,
   13|   patches by alhudz and tonghuaroot, pr848).  Two independent
   14|   quadratic behaviours were fixed:
   15| 
   16|   - ``TokenList.__init__`` called ``str(self)`` which recursively flattened
   17|     the entire token subtree on every group construction.  Deeply nested SQL
   18|     (parentheses, CASE WHEN, subqueries) therefore costs O(n·depth) CPU
   19|     before the depth cap fires — a ~2 KB payload could pin a worker for 10+
   20|     seconds.  Fix: join children's already-cached ``value`` fields directly,
   21|     reducing per-node cost to O(len(tokens)).
   22| 
   23|   - ``group_tokens()`` recomputed ``grp.value = str(start)`` on every extend
   24|     step, re-scanning the entire growing group each time.  Wide flat queries
   25|     (e.g. SELECT with thousands of columns) therefore cost O(N²) in the
   26|     number of columns.  Fix: append only the newly added tokens' values.
   27|

function.name: glob_files
function.description: Recursively list workspace-relative file paths that match a glob, in sorted order. The glob is matched against each file's relative path and against its file name, using Python fnmatch rules, case-sensitive: '*' and '?' also match '/', and '[abc]' matches one listed character. It never matches file contents. Cache and VCS directories (.git, __pycache__, .pytest_cache, .mypy_cache, .ruff_cache, .tox, .venv, node_modules) are skipped.

path.description: Directory (or single file) to list under, relative to the workspace root. Default '.'.

function.name: read_file
function.description: Read a text file with 1-based line numbers. start_line and end_line are inclusive; omit start_line to begin at line 1 and end_line to read to the end. The header reports the range returned and the file's total lines. Long results are shown partially with an output id for paging.

function.name: outline
function.description: List the classes and functions of a Python file with line numbers.

function.name: search_text
function.description: Search file contents for exact text (literal characters, case-sensitive; not a regex). Returns one line per match as path:line: text, with 1-based line numbers, and states the scope searched. file_glob only selects which files are searched.

query.description: Required. The exact text to find, e.g. 'def get_real_name('.

path.description: File or directory to search, relative to the workspace root. Default '.'.

file_glob.description: Optional glob selecting files by relative path or file name (same rules as glob_files), e.g. '*.py'. It never matches file contents. Default '*'.

function.name: replace_text
function.description: Replace exact text in a file. Fails without changing the file if old_text is absent, or if it occurs more than once while replace_all is false; set replace_all to replace every occurrence. Reports how many occurrences were replaced and shows the edited lines.

function.name: write_file
function.description: Create a file, or overwrite it completely if it already exists, with the given content. Missing parent directories are created. Paths are relative to the workspace root.

function.description: Run one command in the workspace root without a shell: no pipes, redirection, chaining (&&, ;), cd, or variable expansion; use workspace-relative paths with forward slashes. 'python' and 'pytest' use the task's Python environment. Shows the command, status (including timeout), exit code, stdout, and stderr; long output is shown partially with an output id for paging. A successful exit does not mean the task is accepted.

function.name: glob_files
function.description: Recursively list workspace-relative file paths that match a glob, in sorted order. The glob is matched against each file's relative path and against its file name, using Python fnmatch rules, case-sensitive: '*' and '?' also match '/', and '[abc]' matches one listed character. It never matches file contents. Cache and VCS directories (.git, __pycache__, .pytest_cache, .mypy_cache, .ruff_cache, .tox, .venv, node_modules) are skipped.

path.description: Directory (or single file) to list under, relative to the workspace root. Default '.'.

function.name: read_file
function.description: Read a text file with 1-based line numbers. start_line and end_line are inclusive; omit start_line to begin at line 1 and end_line to read to the end. The header reports the range returned and the file's total lines. Long results are shown partially with an output id for paging.

function.name: outline
function.description: List the classes and functions of a Python file with line numbers.

function.name: search_text
function.description: Search file contents for exact text (literal characters, case-sensitive; not a regex). Returns one line per match as path:line: text, with 1-based line numbers, and states the scope searched. file_glob only selects which files are searched.

query.description: Required. The exact text to find, e.g. 'def get_real_name('.

path.description: File or directory to search, relative to the workspace root. Default '.'.

file_glob.description: Optional glob selecting files by relative path or file name (same rules as glob_files), e.g. '*.py'. It never matches file contents. Default '*'.

function.name: replace_text
function.description: Replace exact text in a file. Fails without changing the file if old_text is absent, or if it occurs more than once while replace_all is false; set replace_all to replace every occurrence. Reports how many occurrences were replaced and shows the edited lines.

function.name: write_file
function.description: Create a file, or overwrite it completely if it already exists, with the given content. Missing parent directories are created. Paths are relative to the workspace root.

function.name: run
function.description: Run one command in the workspace root without a shell: no pipes, redirection, chaining (&&, ;), cd, or variable expansion; use workspace-relative paths with forward slashes. 'python' and 'pytest' use the task's Python environment. Shows the command, status (including timeout), exit code, stdout, and stderr; long output is shown partially with an output id for paging. A successful exit does not mean the task is accepted.

function.name: read_output
function.description: Read part of an earlier tool result by its output id (for example out_12). Results that were shown partially say which id and range to request. Give start_line/end_line, or start_byte/end_byte for very long lines.

function.name: search_output
function.description: Find lines containing a literal string (plain text, not a regex) in an earlier tool result by its output id.

query.description: Required. The literal text to find.

function.name: history
function.description: Page through authorized durable session history. The response includes a stable next_cursor.

function.name: search_history
function.description: Find literal text in authorized prior actions and observations without knowing an output ID.

function.name: read_artifact
function.description: Read an authorized session artifact by ID, optionally using an exact byte range.

function.name: note
function.description: Save a named plain-text note that persists across turns. Pinned notes are placed in context when space allows.

function.name: read_note
function.description: Read a saved note by name.

function.name: finish
function.description: Declare the work complete. The final workspace is then checked independently.

    1| Development Version
    2| -------------------
    3| 
    4| Notable Changes
    5| 
    6| * Drop support for Python 3.8 and 3.9. Python 3.10+ is now required.
    7| * Migrate project dependencies and environment management from `pixi` to `uv`.
    8| * Replace `flake8` with `ruff` for code checking and linting.
    9| 
   10| Security Fixes
   11| 
   12| * Fix uncontrolled CPU consumption in ``TokenList`` grouping (CWE-1333,
   13|   patches by alhudz and tonghuaroot, pr848).  Two independent
   14|   quadratic behaviours were fixed:
   15| 
   16|   - ``TokenList.__init__`` called ``str(self)`` which recursively flattened
   17|     the entire token subtree on every group construction.  Deeply nested SQL
   18|     (parentheses, CASE WHEN, subqueries) therefore costs O(n·depth) CPU
   19|     before the depth cap fires — a ~2 KB payload could pin a worker for 10+
   20|     seconds.  Fix: join children's already-cached ``value`` fields directly,
   21|     reducing per-node cost to O(len(tokens)).
   22| 
   23|   - ``group_tokens()`` recomputed ``grp.value = str(start)`` on every extend
   24|     step, re-scanning the entire growing group each time.  Wide flat queries
   25|     (e.g. SELECT with thousands of columns) therefore cost O(N²) in the
   26|     number of columns.  Fix: append only the newly added tokens' values.
   27| 
   28| Enhancements
   29| 
   30| * Modernize type annotations in top-level API functions using PEP 585 and PEP 604 syntax.
   31| 
   32| Bug Fixes
   33| 
   34| * Fix statement splitting (issue845).
   35| * Fix a late-binding closure bug in `TokenList.token_not_matching`.
   36| * Recognize ``ROW_FORMAT`` as a keyword so that ``ALTER TABLE ... ROW_FORMAT=...``
   37|   no longer merges the table name and the option into a single identifier
   38|   (issue773).
   39| * Recognize ``MATERIALIZED`` as a keyword so it is parsed and formatted
   40|   consistently in ``CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW`` statements (issue752).
   41|

   44| ----------------------------
   45| 
   46| Bug Fixes
   47| 
   48| * Fix DoS protection to raise SQLParseError instead of silently returning None
   49|   when grouping limits are exceeded (issue827).
   50| * Fix splitting of BEGIN TRANSACTION statements (issue826).

function.name: glob_files
function.description: Recursively list workspace-relative file paths that match a glob, in sorted order. The glob is matched against each file's relative path and against its file name, using Python fnmatch rules, case-sensitive: '*' and '?' also match '/', and '[abc]' matches one listed character. It never matches file contents. Cache and VCS directories (.git, __pycache__, .pytest_cache, .mypy_cache, .ruff_cache, .tox, .venv, node_modules) are skipped.

path.description: Directory (or single file) to list under, relative to the workspace root. Default '.'.

function.name: read_file
function.description: Read a text file with 1-based line numbers. start_line and end_line are inclusive; omit start_line to begin at line 1 and end_line to read to the end. The header reports the range returned and the file's total lines. Long results are shown partially with an output id for paging.

function.name: outline
function.description: List the classes and functions of a Python file with line numbers.

function.name: search_text
function.description: Search file contents for exact text (literal characters, case-sensitive; not a regex). Returns one line per match as path:line: text, with 1-based line numbers, and states the scope searched. file_glob only selects which files are searched.

query.description: Required. The exact text to find, e.g. 'def get_real_name('.

path.description: File or directory to search, relative to the workspace root. Default '.'.

file_glob.description: Optional glob selecting files by relative path or file name (same rules as glob_files), e.g. '*.py'. It never matches file contents. Default '*'.

function.name: replace_text
function.description: Replace exact text in a file. Fails without changing the file if old_text is absent, or if it occurs more than once while replace_all is false; set replace_all to replace every occurrence. Reports how many occurrences were replaced and shows the edited lines.

function.name: write_file
function.description: Create a file, or overwrite it completely if it already exists, with the given content. Missing parent directories are created. Paths are relative to the workspace root.

function.name: run
function.description: Run one command in the workspace root without a shell: no pipes, redirection, chaining (&&, ;), cd, or variable expansion; use workspace-relative paths with forward slashes. 'python' and 'pytest' use the task's Python environment. Shows the command, status (including timeout), exit code, stdout, and stderr; long output is shown partially with an output id for paging.     4| Notable Changes

   10| Security Fixes
   11| 
   12| * Fix uncontrolled CPU consumption in ``TokenList`` grouping (CWE-1333,
   13|   patches by alhudz and tonghuaroot, pr848).  Two independent
   14|   quadratic behaviours were fixed:
   15| 
   16|   - ``TokenList.__init__`` called ``str(self)`` which recursively flattened
   17|     the entire token subtree on every group construction.  Deeply nested SQL
   18|     (parentheses, CASE WHEN, subqueries) therefore costs O(n·depth) CPU
   19|     before the depth cap fires — a ~2 KB payload could pin a worker for 10+
   20|     seconds.  Fix: join children's already-cached ``value`` fields directly,
   21|     reducing per-node cost to O(len(tokens)).
   22| 
   23|   - ``group_tokens()`` recomputed ``grp.value = str(start)`` on every extend
   24|     step, re-scanning the entire growing group each time.  Wide flat queries
   25|     (e.g. SELECT with thousands of columns) therefore cost O(N²) in the
   26|     number of columns.  Fix: append only the newly added tokens' values.

structured_output.content: Found the regression: `TokenList.insert_after` in sqlparse/sql.py has its if/else branches inverted. When there IS a next token, it should insert the new token immediately before that next token (at its index); when there is NO next token, it should append at the end. The current code does the opposite (appends when there's a next token, and tries `self.tokens.insert(None, token)` when there isn't, i.e. using `nidx` which is `None` in that case — though in practice the "next token exists" branch is hit far more often, silently appending tokens at the wrong (end) position instead of right after `where`). This breaks `AlignedIndentFilter._process_parenthesis` (subquery indentation) and `_process_case` (extra whitespace before END) by inserting whitespace/newline tokens at the end of the token list rather than right after the intended token, causing extra indentation/misalignment in aligned reindent output. Fixing the condition so it matches the correct original semantics (append only when there's no next token; otherwise insert before the next token) should restore correct behavior and is a general correctness fix used by other filters too, not just aligned_indent.

message.content: Found the regression: `TokenList.insert_after` in sqlparse/sql.py has its if/else branches inverted. When there IS a next token, it should insert the new token immediately before that next token (at its index); when there is NO next token, it should append at the end. The current code does the opposite (appends when there's a next token, and tries `self.tokens.insert(None, token)` when there isn't, i.e. using `nidx` which is `None` in that case — though in practice the "next token exists" branch is hit far more often, silently appending tokens at the wrong (end) position instead of right after `where`). This breaks `AlignedIndentFilter._process_parenthesis` (subquery indentation) and `_process_case` (extra whitespace before END) by inserting whitespace/newline tokens at the end of the token list rather than right after the intended token, causing extra indentation/misalignment in aligned reindent output. Fixing the condition so it matches the correct original semantics (append only when there's no next token; otherwise insert before the next token) should restore correct behavior and is a general correctness fix used by other filters too, not just aligned_indent.

Found the regression: `TokenList.insert_after` in sqlparse/sql.py has its if/else branches inverted. When there IS a next token, it should insert the new token immediately before that next token (at its index); when there is NO next token, it should append at the end. The current code does the opposite (appends when there's a next token, and tries `self.tokens.insert(None, token)` when there isn't, i.e. using `nidx` which is `None` in that case — though in practice the "next token exists" branch is hit far more often, silently appending tokens at the wrong (end) position instead of right after `where`). This breaks `AlignedIndentFilter._process_parenthesis` (subquery indentation) and `_process_case` (extra whitespace before END) by inserting whitespace/newline tokens at the end of the token list rather than right after the intended token, causing extra indentation/misalignment in aligned reindent output. Fixing the condition so it matches the correct original semantics (append only when there's no next token; otherwise insert before the next token) should restore correct behavior and is a general correctness fix used by other filters too, not just aligned_indent.

function.name: glob_files
function.description: Recursively list workspace-relative file paths that match a glob, in sorted order. The glob is matched against each file's relative path and against its file name, using Python fnmatch rules, case-sensitive: '*' and '?' also match '/', and '[abc]' matches one listed character. It never matches file contents. Cache and VCS directories (.git, __pycache__, .pytest_cache, .mypy_cache, .ruff_cache, .tox, .venv, node_modules) are skipped.

path.description: Directory (or single file) to list under, relative to the workspace root. Default '.'.

function.name: read_file
function.description: Read a text file with 1-based line numbers. start_line and end_line are inclusive; omit start_line to begin at line 1 and end_line to read to the end. The header reports the range returned and the file's total lines. Long results are shown partially with an output id for paging.

function.name: outline
function.description: List the classes and functions of a Python file with line numbers.

function.name: search_text
function.description: Search file contents for exact text (literal characters, case-sensitive; not a regex). Returns one line per match as path:line: text, with 1-based line numbers, and states the scope searched. file_glob only selects which files are searched.

query.description: Required. The exact text to find, e.g. 'def get_real_name('.

path.description: File or directory to search, relative to the workspace root. Default '.'.

file_glob.description: Optional glob selecting files by relative path or file name (same rules as glob_files), e.g. '*.py'. It never matches file contents. Default '*'.

function.name: replace_text
function.description: Replace exact text in a file. Fails without changing the file if old_text is absent, or if it occurs more than once while replace_all is false; set replace_all to replace every occurrence. Reports how many occurrences were replaced and shows the edited lines.

function.name: write_file
function.description: Create a file, or overwrite it completely if it already exists, with the given content. Missing parent directories are created. Paths are relative to the workspace root.

structured_output.content:
I identified and fixed the regression: `TokenList.insert_after` in sqlparse/sql.py had its if/else branches inverted (likely from an accidental refactor). It was supposed to insert the token right before the next non-whitespace token when one exists, and append to the end only when there is no next token. The previous code did the opposite — it appended to the end whenever a next token existed (silently misplacing newly-inserted alignment whitespace/newline tokens), and tried `self.tokens.insert(nidx, token)` with `nidx=None` in the no-next-token case (which would raise, though that branch was rarely hit in practice). This broke `AlignedIndentFilter._process_parenthesis` (subquery re-indentation) and `_process_case` (aligning CASE/WHEN/THEN/ELSE/END), causing the "format reindent aligned" test failures.

I fixed it to:
```python
if next_ is None:
    self.tokens.append(token)
else:
    self.tokens.insert(nidx, token)
```

I verified with several manual checks (basic SELECT/WHERE/AND alignment, CASE statements, CASE with BETWEEN, and a subquery-in-FROM alignment) that output now looks correctly aligned. Let me run one more check with mismatched CASE condition widths (where the inserted alignment whitespace has nonzero length, so the bug is actually visible) to make sure the fix is effective, then finish.

I identified and fixed the regression: `TokenList.insert_after` in sqlparse/sql.py had its if/else branches inverted (likely from an accidental refactor). It was supposed to insert the token right before the next non-whitespace token when one exists, and append to the end only when there is no next token. The previous code did the opposite — it appended to the end whenever a next token existed (silently misplacing newly-inserted alignment whitespace/newline tokens), and tried `self.tokens.insert(nidx, token)` with `nidx=None` in the no-next-token case (which would raise, though that branch was rarely hit in practice). This broke `AlignedIndentFilter._process_parenthesis` (subquery re-indentation) and `_process_case` (aligning CASE/WHEN/THEN/ELSE/END), causing the "format reindent aligned" test failures.

I fixed it to:
```python
if next_ is None:
    self.tokens.append(token)
else:
    self.tokens.insert(nidx, token)
```

I verified with several manual checks (basic SELECT/WHERE/AND alignment, CASE statements, CASE with BETWEEN, and a subquery-in-FROM alignment) that output now looks correctly aligned. Let me run one more check with mismatched CASE condition widths (where the inserted alignment whitespace has nonzero length, so the bug is actually visible) to make sure the fix is effective, then finish.

Found the regression: `TokenList.insert_after` in sqlparse/sql.py has its if/else branches inverted. When there IS a next token, it should insert the new token immediately before that next token (at its index); when there is NO next token, it should append at the end. The current code does the opposite (appends when there's a next token, and tries `self.tokens.insert(None, token)` when there isn't, i.e. using `nidx` which is `None` in that case — though in practice the "next token exists" branch is hit far more often, silently appending tokens at the wrong (end) position instead of right after `where`). This breaks `AlignedIndentFilter._process_parenthesis` (subquery indentation) and `_process_case` (extra whitespace before END) by inserting whitespace/newline tokens at the end of the token list rather than right after the intended token, causing extra indentation/misalignment in aligned reindent output. Fixing the condition so it matches the correct original semantics (append only when there's no next token; otherwise insert before the next token) should restore correct behavior and is a general correctness fix used by other filters too, not just aligned_indent.

I identified and fixed the regression: `TokenList.insert_after` in sqlparse/sql.py had its if/else branches inverted (likely from an accidental refactor). It was supposed to insert the token right before the next non-whitespace token when one exists, and append to the end only when there is no next token. This broke `AlignedIndentFilter._process_parenthesis` (subquery re-indentation) and `_process_case` (aligning CASE/WHEN/THEN/ELSE/END), causing the "format reindent aligned" test failures.

I fixed it to:
```python
if next_ is None:
    self.tokens.append(token)
else:
    self.tokens.insert(nidx, token)
```

I verified with several manual checks (basic SELECT/WHERE/AND alignment, CASE statements, CASE with BETWEEN, and a subquery-in-FROM alignment) that output now looks correctly aligned. structured_output.content:
The regression was in `TokenList.insert_after` (sqlparse/sql.py). Its if/else branches were inverted: it appended the new token to the end of the token list whenever a "next" token existed, and tried to insert at `nidx` (which is `None`) when there wasn't one. This silently misplaced the whitespace/newline tokens that `AlignedIndentFilter` inserts for subquery re-indentation (`_process_parenthesis`) and CASE/WHEN/THEN/ELSE/END alignment (`_process_case`), causing all the "format reindent aligned" test failures (basic, case statement, case statement with between, and others).

Fix applied:
```python
def insert_after(self, where, token, skip_ws=True):
    """Inserts *token* after *where*."""
    if not isinstance(where, int):
        where = self.token_index(where)
    nidx, next_ = self.token_next(where, skip_ws=skip_ws)
    token.parent = self
    if next_ is None:
        self.tokens.append(token)
    else:
        self.tokens.insert(nidx, token)
```

Verified manually with several `reindent_aligned=True` cases (basic SELECT/WHERE/AND, CASE statement, CASE with BETWEEN, CASE with varying condition widths, subquery in FROM, and JOIN/GROUP BY/ORDER BY/LIMIT) — all now produce correctly aligned output matching the expected format (e.g. SELECT column list aligned, FROM/WHERE/AND vertically aligned on keyword right edge, CASE/WHEN/THEN condition padding aligned, subquery indented and closing paren aligned, JOIN/GROUP BY/ORDER BY aligned).

This is a minimal, targeted fix to the inverted conditional; no other code was changed.
